title: Assertion-less Tests (The Silent Pass)
pattern: Test cases that execute a production code path but contain no assertions or validation conditions, relying solely on the absence of a crash (panic) to declare success.
why_bad: It represents a major "coverage theater" smell. The test passes even if the production code returns incorrect data, performs zero actions, or fails to set up state. It provides zero functional confidence [29].
detection: Test functions (`#[test]`) containing zero assertion macros (`assert!`, `assert_eq!`, `should_panic`, etc.) or checking no outputs.
counterexample: A test specifically designed to verify that a complex operation does not panic under exceptional inputs, although even this is better verified with explicit outcome checks.
fix: Add explicit asserts validating the return values, invariants, or state modifications of the operation [29].
source: *   *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, "Testing Code: Silent Passes" (p. 239) [29]
